rationale: Ninth turn: the per-case endpoint names made the contrast measurable (CheckRun a7083e51d44b4b1589eeb21b40848782: non-snapshot case violated, snapshot case holds), and the same harness is now extended with the gap's other half: the captured persistent (RocksDB) backend under the identical request. Run locally first, that third case also aborts, but at a different site - the panic message is 'Error reading from storage.: ErrHelper' raised inside the core crate at omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs:428 (create_log_sync's expect), not the in-memory arithmetic panic, because PersistentStorage::get_suffix returns an error for a request below its compacted prefix instead of the empty suffix its trait specifies. Submitted as a further revision of the same experiment so both halves of the applicability gap are measured.

scope.description: Three scenarios in one test, each driving one responder replica through a legal leader prefix (Prepare, AcceptSync with six entries and decided_idx 6, forwarded Compaction::Trim(6)) and then a legal Prepare with decided_idx 3 and an older accepted round: (a) snapshots disabled with the in-memory backend, (b) snapshots enabled with the in-memory backend, (c) snapshots disabled with the persistent RocksDB backend. The outcome of handling that Prepare is reported per case.
assumptions: The messages delivered are the shapes a real leader produces (Prepare, AcceptSync/log_sync, forwarded Compaction::Trim, and a later Prepare from a node whose decided index lags); the responder is a real OmniPaxos instance whose state is produced by those messages rather than set directly.

The three-node configuration is used only for construction; the responder is node 2 and the sender is node 1. No tick, no election and no message routing are involved, so nothing depends on scheduling.

AcceptSync carries sync_idx 0 with a six-entry suffix and decided_idx 6, i.e. the update a leader sends to a peer that has no entries yet; the forwarded Trim(6) is legal because the responder's decided index is already 6.

The state this harness reaches (accepted_idx 6, decided_idx 6, compacted_idx 6, accepted round newer than the preparing node's) is the same state the earlier multi-node experiment reached through real message exchange.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled, matching the controller's cargo test invocation.

For case (c) the responder uses PersistentStorage opened on a fresh temporary directory, with the same entry type as case (a); the temporary directory is kept alive for the case and dropped afterwards.
Cases (a) and (b) use the in-memory backend behind a shared handle so the same code path is exercised with and without snapshots.
excluded: Release-profile behaviour, the persistent storage backend, and cluster-level consequences after the abort are not measured here.
Only the snapshot/non-snapshot distinction is varied; cluster size, batch size, trim index and quorum are held equal.
Behaviour when overflow checks are disabled (release profile) is not measured for any case.

experiment.prefix: scenario(case, snapshots, outcome_event, store, mk) builds one OmniPaxos instance (pid 2, nodes 1,2,3) over the supplied storage and then calls, in order: handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,1,pid 1), decided_idx: 0, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 0}); handle_incoming(AcceptSync{n: (1,1,pid 1), seq_num: (session 0, counter 1), decided_idx: 6, log_sync: {decided_snapshot: None, suffix: six entries 0..5, sync_idx: 0, stopsign: None}}); handle_incoming(Compaction::Trim(6)). It then emits case_started and state_reached (both carrying case and use_snapshots, plus accepted_idx/decided_idx/compacted_idx on state_reached), and finally calls handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,2,pid 1), decided_idx: 3, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 6}) inside catch_unwind, emitting the case-specific outcome event with case, use_snapshots, outcome, panic message and the three indices. The test runs the prefix three times: 'nosnapshot_entry' (UseSnapshots false, in-memory backend, event log_sync_outcome_nosnapshot), 'snapshot_entry' (UseSnapshots true, in-memory backend, event log_sync_outcome_snapshot) and 'persistent_backend_entry' (UseSnapshots false, PersistentStorage opened on a fresh tempdir, event log_sync_outcome_persistent).
semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the harness only uses the crate's public API and message types. Relative to the previous revision only the emitted identity fields changed (use_snapshots added to state_reached).
experiment.responsibility: The three cases separate which captured component decides the outcome: the core's log-update construction selects its branch from T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() and the deciding node's decided index; with the in-memory backend the abort is raised by its unchecked subtraction inside MemoryStorage::get_suffix, and with the persistent backend the storage returns an error for the same request and the core's own expect in create_log_sync raises the abort.

comparisons.description: Without snapshots, handling the stale node's Prepare completes instead of aborting.
With snapshots enabled, the same request completes, bounding the failure to the non-snapshot configuration.
With the captured persistent backend and no snapshots, handling the stale node's Prepare completes instead of aborting.

knowledge.assertion: the snapshot branch is taken only when use_snapshots() is true and decided_idx > common_prefix_idx; otherwise get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) is used with no comparison against the responder's compacted index

experiment.revision_reason: Third case added for the gap's second half: the identical request is now also exercised against the captured persistent storage backend, with its own endpoint event name (log_sync_outcome_persistent) and its own state admission.
